key_insight: RheOFormer’s failures in steady Bingham channel flow can be reduced through logarithmic velocity representations, gradient-aware losses, and a few targeted training cases.
engineering_relevance: These remedies support data-efficient CFD surrogates for viscoplastic flows with low-gradient plugs and sharp yielded–unyielded transitions.
method: Evaluate RheOFormer across dataset structures, velocity scales, and parameter-space coverage.
Introduce logarithmic velocity representations and gradient-aware losses to improve plug-region predictions.
Add strategically selected training cases covering missing physical regimes.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved accuracy in challenging regimes, reduced extrapolation errors with a few added cases, and accurate steady-state prediction from one partially developed snapshot that outperforms copying the input.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to steady Bingham channel flow; generalization to complex geometries and other rheologies remains unestablished.
paper_title: Failure Modes and Data-Efficient Remedies for Transformer-Based Prediction of Viscoplastic Flows
